description:
# Check: upstream keys.test.ts

## Upstream file
tmp/pi-mono/packages/tui/test/keys.test.ts

## Subject
Keyboard input parsing and key matching across Kitty CSI-u, xterm modifyOtherKeys, and legacy protocols.

## Upstream test count (approx)
108

## Behaviors asserted upstream

Kitty protocol with base layout keys (non-Latin layouts):
- matches Ctrl+c/Ctrl+d/Ctrl+z when pressing Ctrl+Cyrillic-equivalent with base layout key
- matches Ctrl+Shift+p with base layout key
- still matches direct codepoint when no base layout key
- matches super-modified Kitty bindings including combined modifiers
- matches digit bindings via Kitty CSI-u
- normalizes Kitty keypad functional keys to logical digits, symbols, and navigation
- handles shifted key in format (codepoint:shifted:base;modifier)
- handles event type in format (modifier:event)
- handles full format with shifted key, base key, and event type
- prefers codepoint for Latin letters even when base layout differs
- prefers codepoint for symbol keys even when base layout differs
- does not match wrong key even with base layout
- does not match wrong modifiers even with base layout

xterm modifyOtherKeys:
- matches Ctrl+c/d/z
- Enter variants (ctrl+enter, shift+enter, alt+enter)
- Tab variants
- Backspace variants
- Escape
- Space variants
- symbol combos, digit combos
- shifted uppercase letters
- Ctrl+Alt+letter

Legacy encoding:
- legacy Ctrl+c (ASCII 3); Ctrl+d (ASCII 4); escape; linefeed as enter; linefeed as shift+enter when kitty active; Ctrl+space (ASCII 0)
- legacy Ctrl+symbol (e.g., Ctrl+\\, Ctrl+], Ctrl+_)
- legacy Ctrl+Alt+symbol
- raw 0x08 as plain backspace outside Windows Terminal
- raw 0x08 as ctrl+backspace in local Windows Terminal
- raw 0x08 as plain backspace in Windows Terminal over SSH
- legacy alt-prefixed sequences when kitty inactive
- does NOT parse legacy alt-prefixed sequences when kitty active
- arrow keys
- SS3 arrows, home/end
- legacy function keys and clear
- alt+arrows
- rxvt modifier sequences

Decoding helpers:
- decodes Kitty keypad functional keys to printable characters
- decodes printable xterm modifyOtherKeys sequences

Parsing:
- Kitty protocol with alternate keys returning Latin key name
- codepoint preference for Latin/symbol keys when base layout differs
- returns key name from codepoint when no base layout
- shifted uppercase CSI-u letters as shift+letter
- ignores Kitty CSI-u with unsupported modifiers
- legacy Ctrl+letter
- special keys (escape, tab, enter, etc.)
- double bracket pageUp

## Upstream dependencies
decodeKittyPrintable, decodePrintableKey, Key, matchesKey, parseKey, setKittyProtocolActive from ../src/keys.js

## Upstream notes
setKittyProtocolActive() toggles protocol. Windows Terminal 0x08 handling depends on SSH env vars (WT_SESSION, SSH_CONNECTION, SSH_CLIENT, SSH_TTY).

## Candidate Elixir counterpart(s)
- apps/octo_pi_tui/test/octo_pi/tui/key_parser_test.exs
- apps/octo_pi_tui/test/octo_pi/tui/stdin_fsm_test.exs

## Processing protocol
Same as standard check ticket protocol in epic opi-q5k description. Given size (108 tests), compliance work may need to be split by protocol family (Kitty / xterm / legacy). Each compliance ticket must require re-comparison and block opi-q5k.1.

comments.text:
# Audit findings

Upstream: tmp/pi-mono/packages/tui/test/keys.test.ts (108 tests across 9 describes)
Ours: apps/octo_pi_tui/test/octo_pi/tui/key_parser_test.exs (~560 lines across 18 describes)

## Structural mapping

Our 18 describes cover the same conceptual surface as upstream's 9 describes, usually more granularly:

| Upstream describe (# tests) | Our describe(s) |
|---|---|
| parseKey | "printable chars", "named special keys", "legacy CSI sequences", "SS3 sequences", "rxvt modifier sequences", "Ctrl+letter (C0 controls)", "Ctrl+Space (NUL)", "Ctrl+symbol" |
| Legacy key parsing (6) | "legacy CSI sequences" + "alt-prefix legacy (ESC + byte)" |
| Legacy key matching (17) | NOT DIRECTLY MAPPED — see matchesKey gap below |
| modifyOtherKeys matching (13) | "xterm modifyOtherKeys (\e[27;<mod>;<cp>~)" (parse side), matching side NOT MAPPED |
| Kitty protocol with alternate keys (non-Latin layouts) (15) | "Kitty CSI-u — alternate layouts (Cyrillic/Dvorak)" (parse side); matching side NOT MAPPED |
| Kitty protocol with alternate keys (6) | "Kitty CSI-u", "Kitty CSI-u — super modifier", "Kitty CSI-u — keypad functional keys", "Kitty CSI-u — named special keys" |
| matchesKey | NOT MAPPED |
| decodeKittyPrintable (1) | covered implicitly by Kitty CSI-u parse tests; may not have a dedicated test |
| decodePrintableKey (1) | covered implicitly; may not have a dedicated test |

## Major gap: matchesKey

Upstream keys.ts exports two functions: `parseKey(bytes) -> Key` (what our KeyParser.parse does) and `matchesKey(parsedKey, bindingString) -> boolean` (semantic match: "does this key press satisfy binding 'ctrl+shift+p' even when pressed on a Cyrillic layout?"). Our codebase has no `matches_key` equivalent — grep turns up nothing.

The ~30 upstream tests under "Legacy key matching", "modifyOtherKeys matching", and "Kitty protocol with alternate keys (non-Latin layouts)" verify matchesKey's ability to correctly identify key bindings across:
- Cyrillic → Latin base-layout resolution (Ctrl+С matches Ctrl+c via base layout key)
- Modifier combinations (Ctrl+Shift+p with base layout key)
- xterm modifyOtherKeys Ctrl+letter / Enter / Tab / Backspace / Escape / Space / symbols / digits / shifted uppercase
- Legacy Ctrl+letter (ASCII 1-26) / Ctrl+symbol / Ctrl+Alt+letter / Ctrl+Alt+symbol
- Shifted keys, super modifier combos, event types (press/release/repeat)
- "Prefers codepoint for Latin letters even when base layout differs"

Our KeyParser produces Key structs but does not expose a matcher — downstream code (like Keybindings) likely compares Key struct fields directly. Upstream's matchesKey does stringly-typed binding matching with layout awareness.

## Minor gap: Windows Terminal 0x08 handling

Upstream 3 tests: raw 0x08 maps to backspace normally, to ctrl+backspace in local Windows Terminal (WT_SESSION set, no SSH_* env vars), back to backspace in Windows Terminal over SSH (any of WT_SESSION + SSH_CONNECTION/SSH_CLIENT/SSH_TTY set). Our code: `grep WT_SESSION apps/octo_pi_tui` returns nothing — not implemented. See opi-q5k.4 cross-ref? (no, different file).

## MAPPED (categorical)

Parse-side coverage for: legacy CSI, SS3, rxvt, Kitty CSI-u (press/release/event-type), xterm modifyOtherKeys parse, legacy Ctrl+letter/symbol, arrow keys, function keys (F1..F12), named special keys, bracketed paste markers, alt-prefix legacy (ESC+byte, ESC+symbol, ESC+ctrl combos).

## UNMAPPED

- **matchesKey function + ~30 matching tests** (Cyrillic/base layout, modifier combos, modifyOtherKeys matching, Kitty alternate-key matching).
- Windows Terminal 0x08 handling (3 tests, env-dependent).
- Dedicated decodeKittyPrintable / decodePrintableKey tests (2 tests) — add if our equivalents exist as standalone functions.
- Prefers-codepoint-for-Latin invariant (parse side is present, but matching side is not).
- Super-modifier Kitty matching (parse is present; matching absent).
- Digit CSI-u matching.

## Action

Compliance ticket: (a) implement Key.matches?/2 (or OctoPi.TUI.Keys.matches_key/2) mirroring upstream semantics (Latin/base-layout resolution, string binding parsing), (b) add Windows Terminal 0x08 handling, (c) port the ~30 matching tests + 3 WT tests + 2 decode tests.
